subsystem: Console screens + data layer (packages/web screens, console REST projection, the one SSE channel)
summary: Fifteen routed screens over a thin console REST projection, one SSE channel, and TanStack Query as the only client cache. The single idea that makes it leaner than mcphub: the console never polls and never holds its own state — one cookie-authenticated `GET /api/events` stream carries five frame types, and exactly one rule decides what each does to the cache (status/sync patch, changed/call invalidate, log bypasses Query entirely). That deletes mcphub's five nested providers, its 1202-line SettingsContext, its 3s×60-then-30s ServerContext poller (ServerContext:28-38) and its fetch interceptor. Two more collapses follow: Settings is generated from one annotated zod schema that simultaneously validates the PATCH, renders the form, and feeds search and the palette — replacing a 3928-line accordion; context cost is a `SUM()` over a token count persisted on each tool row at cache time rather than a live recompute (contextCostService.ts:76-95). Authorization has one axis: humans get three global roles, scope lives on API keys, which erases mcphub's owner/visibility/sharedWithUsers matrix and the two divergent filters that disagree about it (dataService.ts:6-28 vs :171).
phase: v1 / MVP. Lands after the core registry and call path exist; every console endpoint is a projection over them plus the two read-model tables defined here. No screen blocks on another screen.

decisions.decision: ONE SSE endpoint `GET /api/events?topics=&server=&level=`, authenticated by the better-auth session cookie only (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax). No token in any URL. API-key consumers get no SSE and poll `GET /api/logs?since=` / `GET /api/activity?before=` with Authorization: Bearer.
decisions.rationale: EventSource cannot set headers and the console is same-origin with the API in a one-process deployment, so the cookie rides along with zero code. mcphub put the JWT in the query string (services/logService.ts:82) and also accepts `?token=` on every route (middlewares/auth.ts:178-180), which lands credentials in access logs, proxy logs and browser history.
decisions.cost: `mcprouter logs -f` is a 1s poll, not push. Ceiling: add a fetch()+ReadableStream variant of the same handler that accepts Bearer; the frame shape does not change.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub: one SSE connection multiplexing the log tail and embedding-sync progress, admin-gated, JWT in the query string; server status dots are POLLED not pushed.

decisions.decision: One cache-consistency rule, no exceptions: `status` and `sync` PATCH the cache via setQueryData; `changed` and `call` INVALIDATE with refetchType:'active'; `log` never touches Query.
decisions.rationale: Patch only where the frame is a complete authoritative replacement of a known slice — a status frame is exactly the row a refetch would return, and during startup these arrive faster than a refetch could keep up. Everywhere else the frame is a signal, not a value, and a wrong patch is worse than an extra GET.
decisions.cost: The status frame's field set is a contract; if the engine ever emits a partial the fleet row silently diverges. Enforced by the frame type owning those fields and nothing else.

decisions.decision: Settings is generated from ONE zod 4 schema annotated via a `z.registry<SettingMeta>()`. The same schema validates `PATCH /api/settings` on the server and, walked on the client, produces the routed section form, the search index and the cmdk entries. Routes are `/settings/:section#<dotted.path>`; dirty state is a diff object against the fetched value; navigate-away uses react-router `useBlocker`.
decisions.rationale: Three consumers, one definition — the alternative is mcphub's schema-in-three-places. Deep link, search and per-setting help fall out for free because every setting already has an id and a meta record.
decisions.cost: A control zod meta cannot describe (the tool-selection tree) needs an explicit escape hatch rather than growing the meta vocabulary.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: SettingsPage.tsx 3928 lines, 11 accordion sections, no search, no deep link; SettingsContext 1202 lines with ~15 near-identical PUT savers.

decisions.decision: Add-server is a routed 3-step wizard (`/servers/new?step=source|configure|verify`) that persists NOTHING until Verify→Save. Step 3 runs an ephemeral probe (`POST /api/servers/probe`, 30s TTL) whose connect logs stream over the same SSE channel under `server: "probe:<id>"`.
decisions.rationale: A failed add must never leave a broken row in the fleet, and the operator must see the real connect output before committing. Transport (streamable vs SSE) is auto-detected by the probe instead of being a radio the user has to get right.
decisions.cost: Probe holds an upstream connection for up to 30s per attempt. Manual transport override lives under Advanced on step 2.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: ServerForm.tsx 2300 lines, one modal, type radio stdio/sse/streamable-http/openapi, ~6 collapsible sections, saves immediately.

decisions.decision: `/triage` is its own screen answering "which upstream is slow or failing right now, and which client is causing it?", backed by two SQL statements over `call_event` (live window, true p95) and `call_rollup_1m` (24h baseline, sparkline). The 1-minute rollup row is upserted in the SAME transaction as the call row.
decisions.rationale: An upsert in the existing write path costs one extra statement and removes the need for any job runner, cron or worker. True p95 over a bounded 15m window with a `(server, started_at desc)` index is cheap at team scale; the baseline only needs a mean.
decisions.cost: Baseline comparison is mean-vs-mean and is labelled "avg", not p95. Upgrade: t-digest column or timescaledb when the window must exceed 15m.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub has no /metrics, no tracing, no per-tool latency histograms and its docs punt to an external APM; /health returns 200 "degraded" when servers are down (healthController.ts:32-46).

decisions.decision: Authorization has one axis. Humans have three global roles (viewer / operator / admin) checked as route-group middleware. Everything scoped — which servers and groups may be reached — is scoped on the API KEY, using better-auth apiKey `permissions`. No per-resource owner/visibility/sharedWith on servers or groups in v1.
decisions.rationale: Team self-host means the operators already trust each other to read the fleet; what needs containment is the machine credential a CI runner holds. One axis cannot disagree with itself.
decisions.cost: A team wanting a viewer restricted to some groups must wait. Upgrade: add `group.owner` plus a single read/manage predicate; the key-scope model is unaffected.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: Every Server/Group carries owner/visibility/sharedWithUsers (entities/Server.ts:45-57) with TWO divergent authz paths that disagree (dataService.ts:6-28 vs DaoConfigService.filterSettingsForUser:171 where owner===undefined is visible to everyone), plus group.visibility==null opening the route to any authenticated caller (utils/groupAccess.ts:6).

decisions.decision: Context cost is a persisted integer. The engine writes `tool.tokens` (cl100k of JSON.stringify({name,description,inputSchema})) at cache time, alongside the namespaced `<server><sep><tool>` name. `GET /api/cost` is a SUM/GROUP BY; the group editor's live token meter sums client-side from data it already has.
decisions.rationale: The count is computed once per tool version instead of on every request, and the group-builder meter needs no endpoint at all. Only the Smart Routing meta-tool cost stays server-computed, because its description embeds the live server list and so varies by scope.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: contextCostService.ts aggregates live on every call with no persistence; useCostData is manually re-triggered on every server/group change.

decisions.decision: The group editor is a two-pane editor (not a wizard) with a "Preview as client" action that renders the literal `tools/list` payload the group would return, alias substitution applied.
decisions.rationale: Groups are edited far more often than created, so a wizard is friction. Alias substitution at projection time (mcpService.ts:3311-3341) is the single most invisible behaviour in the product and the thing operators get wrong; showing the actual payload is cheaper than documenting it.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: ServerToolConfig.tsx:378-570 has the selection tree but no way to see the resulting projection.

decisions.decision: The tool explorer's invoke console posts to `POST /api/tools/:server/:tool/invoke`, which runs the identical core call path as a real MCP request — including the call-time enable check — and records a `call_event` with `principal_kind='console'`.
decisions.rationale: A test surface that bypasses the enable gate would report success for a tool a client cannot reach, which is exactly the class mcphub's CVE fix closed. Recording console calls keeps triage honest about who generated load.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: Reproduces mcphub's afcc72f fix: the execution-time gate inside findToolOnServer (mcpService.ts:3388) checked under both bare and prefixed keys, and ToolUnavailableError (:2654) giving identical text for hidden and missing.

interfaces.name: routes.tsx — SPA route table
interfaces.notes: Every screen is a route; there are no modal-only surfaces except confirm dialogs. Inspectors are `?sel=` search params on the list route so they are shareable and Back closes them. Role column is the minimum role; the guard is one `<RequireRole>` wrapper per group, not per screen.

interfaces.name: packages/web/src/lib/qk.ts — query key factory, staleTime table, invalidation map
interfaces.notes: Array prefixes are the whole design: `['servers']` invalidates the list, every detail and every tool list under it. Filters are serialised into the key as the object itself (TanStack hashes it deterministically) so a URL param change is a new key, not a manual refetch.
interfaces.sketch:
export const qk = {
  me:          ()                       => ['me'] as const,
  fleet:       ()                       => ['fleet'] as const,
  servers:     ()                       => ['servers'] as const,
  server:      (n: string)              => ['servers', n] as const,
  serverTools: (n: string)              => ['servers', n, 'tools'] as const,
  serverHealth:(n: string, w: Window)   => ['servers', n, 'health', w] as const,
  probe:       (id: string)             => ['probe', id] as const,
  groups:      ()                       => ['groups'] as const,
  group:       (s: string)              => ['groups', s] as const,
  groupPreview:(s: string)              => ['groups', s, 'preview'] as const,
  tools:       (f: ToolFilter)          => ['tools', f] as const,
  tool:        (q: string)              => ['tools', 'one', q] as const,
  triage:      (w: Window)              => ['metrics', 'triage', w] as const,
  callers:     (n: string, w: Window)   => ['metrics', 'callers', n, w] as const,
  toolStats:   (q: string, w: Window)   => ['metrics', 'tool', q, w] as const,
  cost:        ()                       => ['cost'] as const,
  activity:    (f: ActivityFilter)      => ['activity', f] as const,
  activityOne: (id: string)             => ['activity', 'one', id] as const,
  logs:        (f: LogFilter)           => ['logs', f] as const,        // useInfiniteQuery, history only
  keys:        ()                       => ['keys'] as const,
  users:       ()                       => ['users'] as const,
  settings:    ()                       => ['settings'] as const,
  catalog:     (q: string)              => ['catalog', q] as const,
  embeddings:  ()                       => ['embeddings'] as const,
};

// staleTime by key prefix. Nothing has refetchInterval except ['metrics'].
export const STALE: Record<string, number> = {
  me: Infinity,          // invalidated only by login/logout
  settings: 300_000,
  servers: 30_000, groups: 30_000, keys: 30_000, users: 30_000,
  tools: 60_000, cost: 60_000, fleet: 30_000, embeddings: 30_000,
  metrics: 10_000,       // + refetchInterval 15_000, refetchIntervalInBackground: false
  activity: 0,
  logs: Infinity,        // cursor pages are immutable
  catalog: 600_000,
  probe: 0,              // state arrives over SSE; never polled
};

export const qc = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: {
  staleTime: (q) => STALE[q.queryKey[0] as string] ?? 30_000,
  gcTime: 300_000,
  refetchOnWindowFocus: true,
  retry: (n, e: any) => n < 2 && (e?.status === undefined || e.status >= 500),
}}});

// mutation -> invalidate. Always in onSettled, never onSuccess: a mutation that
// failed after partially applying must still resync.
export const INVALIDATES: Record<string, readonly unknown[][]> = {
  'POST   /api/servers':                  [qk.servers(), qk.fleet(), qk.tools({}), qk.cost()],
  'PATCH  /api/servers/:n':               [qk.servers(), qk.fleet(), qk.tools({}), qk.cost()],
  'DELETE /api/servers/:n':               [qk.servers(), qk.fleet(), qk.tools({}), qk.cost(), qk.groups()],
  'POST   /api/servers/:n/restart':       [],   // optimistic state='connecting'; SSE status frame settles it
  'POST   /api/servers/:n/sleep|wake':    [],   // same
  'POST   /api/servers/:n/secrets':       [qk.server('$n')],
  'PATCH  /api/tools/:s/:t':              [qk.serverTools('$s'), qk.tools({}), qk.cost()],
  'POST   /api/tools/:s/:t/invoke':       [],   // result is not cached; the call frame debounce-bumps ['metrics']
  'POST|PATCH /api/groups/:slug':         [qk.groups(), qk.cost()],
  'DELETE /api/groups/:slug':             [qk.groups(), qk.cost()],
  'PATCH  /api/settings':                 [qk.settings()],  // + ['tools'],['cost'] if patch touches routing.*
                                                            // + ['embeddings']  if it touches embeddings.*
  'POST|DELETE /api/keys':                [qk.keys()],
  'POST|PATCH  /api/users':               [qk.users()],
  'POST   /api/market/:id/install':       [],   // navigates to the wizard; nothing is written yet
};
// Another operator's write reaches this browser as an SSE `changed` frame and
// invalidates the same prefix. Echo-suppression of our own write is skipped:
// a duplicate invalidate is one extra GET and zero lines of code.

interfaces.name: packages/server/src/events/envelope.ts — the one SSE channel
interfaces.kind: TypeScript (shared type, Hono handler, client demux)
interfaces.notes: All frames ride the default `message` event with a discriminated union, not named SSE events, so adding a type is one union member and one switch arm instead of a new addEventListener on every client. `Last-Event-ID` resume applies HERE and only here — this is a plain web API, not an MCP endpoint, so the 2026-07-28 removal of SSE resumability is irrelevant to it.

interfaces.name: /triage — "which upstream is slow or failing right now, and which client is causing it?"
interfaces.notes: Three bands, above the fold at 1280×800, no scroll needed to read the verdict. Row select is a URL param (`?server=`) so a triage state is pasteable into chat. The right rail is the ONLY live-moving element; bands 1-2 refresh on the 15s metrics interval plus the debounced call-frame bump.
interfaces.sketch:
┌ TRIAGE                                    window [15m ▾]  ⟳ 4s ago ──────────┐
│ BAND 1 — verdict (0-3 rows, server-computed sentences, or "All nominal")     │
│  ● github-mcp   avg 3.1s vs 0.52s baseline (6.0×)  ·  err 4%                 │
│                 62% of its time from key ci-runner (claude-code/1.4)  [open] │
│  ● notion       err 31% (47/152)  ·  AUTH_REQUIRED since 14:02       [fix →] │
├ BAND 2 — fleet latency matrix (rows = servers with calls in window) ─────────┤
│ ●  server        calls  err%   p95     avg Δ      last 60m                   │
│ ●  github-mcp     412   4.0%  8.4s   3.1s ▲6.0×  ▁▁▂▃▅███▇▅  ← selected      │
│ ●  fs-local      1 204   0.0%  41ms   12ms  ▬1.0×  ▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁                │
│ ●  notion          152  31.0%  2.1s   0.9s ▲1.8×  ▁▂█████▇██                 │
├ BAND 3 — attribution for the selected server ────────────┬ LIVE CALLS ───────┤
│ caller                client        calls err%  p95  share│ 14:22:07 ok  41ms│
│ key ci-runner         claude-code   256  6.2% 9.1s  62% ██│ 14:22:07 err 8.2s│
│ user ana@x.io         cursor         98  1.0% 3.2s  22% █ │ 14:22:06 ok  120ms│
│ key readonly-bot      -              58  0.0% 1.1s  16% ▌ │ (SSE `call` ring) │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┘
Actions: [open server] [open filtered activity] [open filtered logs] [restart]
         [rate-limit this key →/keys] [disable this tool]
Empty:   "No calls in the last 15m." + window widener. Bands 2/3 hidden, band 1 shows "All nominal".
Loading: bands render at final height with em-dash cells; the sparkline column is a flat rule.
Error:   last payload stays, dimmed, with "metrics stale — 14:19:40" in band 1's slot.

-- GET /api/triage?window=15m  (band 1 + band 2). $1 = window interval.
WITH live AS (
  SELECT server,
         count(*)::int                                                    AS n,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE status <> 'ok')::int                      AS n_err,
         avg(duration_ms)::int                                            AS avg_ms,
         (percentile_disc(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY duration_ms))::int AS p95_ms,
         sum(duration_ms)::bigint                                         AS total_ms,
         max(started_at)                                                  AS last_at
  FROM call_event WHERE started_at >= now() - $1::interval GROUP BY server
), base AS (                       -- 24h baseline from the rollup, never from raw rows
  SELECT server, (sum(sum_ms) / NULLIF(sum(n),0))::int AS avg_ms
  FROM call_rollup_1m
  WHERE bucket >= now() - interval '24 hours' AND bucket < now() - $1::interval
  GROUP BY server
), top_caller AS (                 -- the "who" half of the question, ranked by time contributed
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (server) server, principal_label, client_name,
         count(*)::int AS n, sum(duration_ms)::bigint AS total_ms
  FROM call_event WHERE started_at >= now() - $1::interval
  GROUP BY server, principal_label, client_name
  ORDER BY server, sum(duration_ms) DESC
)
SELECT l.server, l.n, l.n_err, l.avg_ms, l.p95_ms, l.last_at,
       b.avg_ms AS baseline_ms,
       round(l.avg_ms::numeric / NULLIF(b.avg_ms,0), 1)  AS slowdown,
       round(l.n_err::numeric / l.n, 3)                  AS err_rate,
       c.principal_label, c.client_name,
       round(c.total_ms::numeric / NULLIF(l.total_ms,0), 2) AS caller_share
FROM live l LEFT JOIN base b USING (server) LEFT JOIN top_caller c USING (server)
ORDER BY err_rate DESC, slowdown DESC NULLS LAST, l.p95_ms DESC
LIMIT 50;
-- sparkline: SELECT server, bucket, n, n_err, (sum_ms/NULLIF(n,0))::int avg_ms
--            FROM call_rollup_1m WHERE bucket >= now() - interval '60 minutes';

-- GET /api/triage/callers?server=&window=  (band 3, fired on row select)
SELECT principal_kind, principal_id, principal_label, client_name, client_version,
       count(*)::int n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status<>'ok')::int n_err,
       (percentile_disc(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY duration_ms))::int p50_ms,
       (percentile_disc(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY duration_ms))::int p95_ms,
       sum(duration_ms)::bigint total_ms
FROM call_event WHERE server = $1 AND started_at >= now() - $2::interval
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY total_ms DESC LIMIT 25;

interfaces.name: packages/server/src/db/observability.ts — the read model
interfaces.notes: Owned by this subsystem; the engine writes both rows in ONE transaction at the end of every call. No job runner. Retention is enforced by a DELETE on the same 60s tick that a settings value controls — mcphub required a manual `DELETE /api/activities/cleanup?daysOld=`.

interfaces.name: /servers/new — add-server wizard (3 steps, nothing persisted until Save)
interfaces.notes: Replaces ServerForm.tsx (2300 lines, one modal). The draft is one object in route state; the URL carries only `?step=`. Marketplace install and JSON-paste import both enter at step 2 with the draft prefilled — one flow, three doors.
interfaces.sketch:
STEP 1  /servers/new?step=source        "Where does this server come from?"
  Four cards, one click each:
    [ Command ]  stdio: a single command line, pasted whole (`npx -y @x/y --flag`)
    [ URL ]      remote: one URL field. Transport is PROBED, not asked — POST an
                 initialize; 200 json/sse => streamable-http, 405/404 => try SSE.
                 Detected transport shown as a mono chip, overridable on step 2.
    [ OpenAPI ]  spec URL or pasted document; SSRF-guarded fetch with per-redirect
                 validation, same guard as the engine.
    [ Marketplace ] inline catalog search; picking an entry fills command/env and jumps to 2.
  error: probe failure is shown inline under the field with the real transport error text,
         not "invalid URL". Step 2 is still reachable (Advanced can override).

STEP 2  /servers/new?step=configure     "What does it need to run?"
  name*      mono input. REJECTED (not warned) if it fails ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$,
             contains the active namespace separator, or collides case-insensitively
             with an existing server. [mcphub only WARNS: mcpService.ts:1710, so two
             names differing by separator chars can alias.]
  env/headers  key/value rows. ${VAR} typed into a value shows a live chip
             resolved / MISSING from GET /api/env/probe?names= — which returns
             BOOLEANS ONLY, never a value.
  secrets    a separate write-only field group; on Save it posts to
             POST /api/servers/:name/secrets. No GET ever returns one.
  Advanced ▸ transport override · request timeout · keepalive · start-on-demand +
             idle TTL · per-session client · proxy.

STEP 3  /servers/new?step=verify        "Does it work, and what will it cost?"
  POST /api/servers/probe -> {probeId}. Ephemeral client, 30s TTL, NOT persisted.
  ┌ connect log (live, SSE topic=log&server=probe:<id>) ─────────────┐
  │ 14:31:02 info  spawn npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github  │
  │ 14:31:04 info  listed 26 tools, 0 prompts, 3 resources           │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ┌ discovered tools  [all] [none]        exposed 26/26 · 18,240 tok ┐
  │ ☑ github-create_issue          412 tok                           │
  │ ☑ github-search_code         1,108 tok                           │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  [Back]                                      [Save server] (operator+)
  Save = ONE transaction: server row + per-tool enabled flags + tokens.
  Failure at step 3 leaves the fleet untouched; the wizard stays open with the log.

EDIT: /servers/:name/config is the SAME step-2 form rendered flat (no wizard),
      plus a [Re-probe] that runs step 3's panel in place.

Only the Smart Routing saving line calls the server, because meta-tool descriptions embed the live server list so their cost varies by scope (smartRoutingService.ts:302).

  Each row is a real <input type=checkbox> with aria-checked="mixed" for the parent.
A tool disabled at the SERVER level renders struck-through, unselectable, with a
  link to /servers/github-mcp/tools — a group cannot re-enable it.

Dirty:   same footer-bar + useBlocker contract as Settings.
/groups (list): one card per group — name, slug (mono), server count, exposed
  tools, exposed tokens, calls 24h, endpoint copy button. Actions: new, duplicate,

interfaces.name: /settings/:section — routed, searchable, deep-linkable settings from one zod schema
interfaces.notes: One schema is the server validator, the form renderer, the search index and the cmdk source. Replaces SettingsPage.tsx (3928 lines) and SettingsContext (1202 lines, ~15 near-identical PUT savers) with one PATCH taking a partial.

interfaces.name: Screen catalog — every remaining screen
interfaces.notes: GLOBAL STATE CONVENTIONS, stated once, deviations noted per screen. LOADING: skeletons at final geometry (8 rows for a table), never a spinner, never a layout shift; numbers render as em-dashes. ERROR: the last good data stays on screen dimmed under a banner with the HTTP status and [Retry]; never a blank page. 401 -> /login?next=. 403 -> inline "your role (viewer) cannot do this", no retry button. EMPTY: one sentence plus exactly one primary action.
interfaces.sketch:
/  FLEET — "Is every upstream connected, and is anything degrading?"
   data  GET /api/fleet: counts {connected/total, toolsExposed/gross, callsPerMin, errRate15m}
         + rows {name, state, transport, toolsExposed/Gross, p95_15m, errRate, lastCallAt,
                 since, spark[60]}. Live-patched by SSE `status`.
   shows dense 32px rows sorted by attention (error > auth_required > connecting > sleeping > ok),
         then name. 4 header numbers, each a link to the screen that explains it.
         Right rail: live tail of status changes + errors only.
   acts  restart · sleep/wake · disable · copy endpoint · multi-select bulk restart/disable
         (mcphub has no bulk actions) · [+ Add server]
   empty "No upstreams yet." [Add server]  (secondary: Browse marketplace)

/servers/:name  DETAIL — "Is this server healthy, and what is it doing?"
   tabs  index | tools | logs | calls | config
   index status dot + state + since + lastError verbatim in mono; transport chip;

deferred.item: Multi-replica event bus (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY or Redis) behind `bus.subscribe`
deferred.add_when: The deployment stops being one process. Until then the in-process ring IS the monotonic seq; the frame shape does not change.

deferred.item: Per-group ownership / ACL for human accounts
deferred.add_when: A team needs a viewer who may see only some groups. Adds `group.owner` plus one read/manage predicate; API-key scoping is unaffected.

deferred.item: True p95 baselines (t-digest column, or timescaledb)
deferred.add_when: The 15m raw-window scan exceeds ~50ms, or triage needs a 24h window. Today the baseline is a mean and is labelled "avg".
A headless consumer needs push instead of the 1s poll on /api/logs. One extra handler branch, same frames.

deferred.item: Saved triage views and threshold alerting (webhook/Slack)
deferred.add_when: Someone asks to be paged instead of looking. The triage SQL is already the predicate.

deferred.item: Responsive layout below 768px (drawer nav, stacked triage bands)
deferred.add_when: Someone actually triages from a phone. Floor for v1: fully usable at 1024px, keyboard and screen-reader complete at every width.

risks: The `status` frame is a contract: it must carry the FULL set of fields it owns (state, toolsExposed, toolsGross, lastError, since). An engine change that emits a partial silently desyncs the fleet row with no error anywhere.
The SSE ring and its Last-Event-ID resume assume a single process. A second replica splits the stream and each browser sees half the events, with no visible failure.

Triage computes true p95 over raw `call_event`; without the `(server, started_at desc)` index, or with a window widened past 15m, the query degrades from indexed to a seq scan under exactly the load it exists to diagnose.

The zod-derived settings form can only render controls the meta vocabulary describes. Pressure to add `control: 'tree' | 'matrix' | ...` would rebuild the 3928-line accordion inside a schema; the escape hatch must stay a plain custom component keyed by path.

The 2s debounce on metrics invalidation means the live call tail visibly moves while the triage numbers sit still. Operators may read the two as contradicting each other; the refresh age must be printed next to the window selector.
security: `GET /api/events` accepts ONLY the better-auth session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax). No credential appears in any URL, so nothing lands in access logs, proxy logs or browser history — mcphub streams logs at `/logs/stream?token=<jwt>` (services/logService.ts:82) and accepts `?token=` on every route (middlewares/auth.ts:178-180).

No CORS headers on any `/api/*` response, so cross-origin EventSource and fetch reads are blocked by the browser and SameSite=Lax keeps the cookie off cross-site subresource requests. mcphub hardcodes `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on spec responses (openApiController.ts:28).
Log and event filtering is SERVER-SIDE. A viewer scoped away from a server never receives its log lines; filtering in the browser would ship them anyway.

`POST /api/tools/:s/:t/invoke` runs the identical core call path including the call-time enable check, so a tool hidden by config returns the identical 'unknown tool' text from the console as from a client — reproducing mcphub's afcc72f fix (gate at mcpService.ts:3388, identical text via ToolUnavailableError :2654). A test console that bypassed the gate would be a disclosure oracle.

Secrets are write-only in the UI: values go to `POST /api/servers/:name/secrets` and no endpoint ever returns one. The `${VAR}` resolution chip reads `GET /api/env/probe?names=` which returns booleans only, never values — mcphub stores env/headers and upstream OAuth tokens in plaintext (oauthSettingsStore.ts:107-129).

The activity inspector distinguishes 'payload not stored' from an empty payload, so an operator cannot mistake a retention policy for a call that sent nothing. Payloads are stored verbatim when enabled and that setting is marked danger in the schema.

Role checks are route-group middleware (`requireRole('viewer')` on every read, `'operator'` on writes, `'admin'` on users and settings), never per-handler, so a new endpoint added inside a group cannot ship unguarded by omission.

Server names are REJECTED, not warned, when they collide case-insensitively or contain the active namespace separator — mcphub only warns (mcpService.ts:1710), allowing two servers whose namespaced tool names alias each other.

Destructive actions (delete server, revoke key, change the namespace separator) require typing the identifier; the last admin cannot be demoted or disabled and the server returns 409 rather than relying on the UI hiding the control.

Every hand-rolled dialog is focus-trapped with Esc-to-dismiss and the tri-state tool tree uses real checkbox inputs with aria-checked="mixed" — mcphub uses native alert()/confirm(), has near-zero aria-* on Settings/Groups/Market, and puts a custom switch on a <button> with no role="switch".
